title: Append-Only Segment Compaction Starvation
pattern: A storage component is designed strictly to append updates to a log file to achieve peak write performance, without implementing any background compaction or segment merging.
why_bad: Locally, the append-only write path is blazingly fast because it avoids all random disk seeks. Globally, it is a system trap. It causes massive read amplification (readers must scan the entire log to find the latest value of a key) and space amplification (stale records accumulate indefinitely). Eventually, the storage device fills up (e.g., SSD garbage collection penalty), causing the whole system to plunge into extremely low performance or crash.
detection: Append-only log storage designs that lack any background thread or scheduler for log compaction, vacuuming, or segment merging.
counterexample: Valid for short-lived sessions or simple transient append-only metrics loggers where space is bounded and reads are rare. Mark `Context-dependent`.
source: Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 7, "Log-Structured Storage: Read/Write Amplification" (p. 129, 143-144).
